We first study the dependence of the scalar QNM frequency (QNF) on the scalar mass and black hole parameters. For angular number $l=0$, a small scalar mass can give rise to a slowly decaying mode which is purely imaginary, while it will become complex for large enough scalar mass and we call it dS-like mode. We also find that the black hole charge and cosmological constant affect the QNM spectrum in qualitatively opposite ways. We then examine SCC under massless and massive scalar perturbations. For massless perturbations, the QNMs spectrum can be organized into photon sphere (PS), de Sitter (dS) and near-extremal (NE) families. Compared with the SCC in the Reissner-Nordström-de Sitter (RN-dS) case, SCC is generally more easily violated in the ABGB-dS spacetime, although this tendency is reversed for sufficiently large cosmological constant. For massive scalar perturbations, we find that the scalar mass does not restore SCC. Instead, it can enhance the violation by driving the system into the regime $\beta>1$. At last, we discuss what we may expect from the violation of SCC in a regular black hole spacetime.
papers.comments: 35 pages, 7 figures, accepted for publication in Physical Review D

papers.title: Variations in the 3.3 $μ$m Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Feature Across Nearby Galaxies Driven by Metallicity and Radiation Field Spectrum
papers.abstract: We use JWST NIRCam imaging to investigate the 3.3 ${\mu}$m polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) feature in nearby galaxies. NIRCam observations of the 3.3 ${\mu}$m feature are emerging as a powerful tool for studying the structure of the interstellar medium (ISM) and the conditions of the dust at ~0".1 resolution. These maps require accurate subtraction of the underlying continuum emission. We present an empirical method to isolate the PAH-correlated emission in the F335M filter using the F300M and F360M filters for continuum subtraction. We find that the slope of the F335M/F300M versus F360M/F300M colors for PAH-correlated emission shows a dependence on local ISM properties, with the strongest dependence on specific star formation rate. Weaker emission features captured by these bands appear suppressed relative to the main 3.3 ${\mu}$m feature in regions of active star formation. We find trends in the 3.3/7.7 and 3.3/11.3 ${\mu}$m ratios that suggest changes in PAH size, charge, and heating by a varying radiation field spectrum. We find decreases in both band ratios with increasing metallicity, which we attribute to a shift to smaller PAH populations at low metallicity. Comparison to optical ionized gas line ratios and dust models show that variations in the interstellar radiation field spectrum influence the PAH feature ratios. This analysis supports inhibited growth formation scenarios for the observed PAH band ratio trends with metallicity and emphasizes the importance of considering the local radiation field characteristics and gas-phase metallicity when using these band ratios as PAH property diagnostics.
papers.comments: 39 pages, 24 figures, 3 tables; accepted for publication in ApJ

papers.title: photo-3x2-pt: Cosmology from cosmic shear and galaxy clustering with a single photometric galaxy catalog
papers.abstract: We perform a joint cosmological analysis using angular power spectra of galaxy clustering, galaxy-shear cross correlation, and cosmic shear (hereafter referred to as photo-3x2-pt) measured from the Hyper Suprime-Cam year-3 (HSC-Y3) weak lensing shape catalog. We employ the pseudo-$C_\ell$ method to measure these power spectra and use the template deprojection method to mitigate systematics in the galaxy density maps. We perform a standard Bayesian likelihood analysis for cosmological inference based on the measured photo-3x2-pt, including contributions from intrinsic alignments of galaxies, galaxy clustering bias, lensing magnification effect, baryonic feedback effect, and source redshift distribution errors. For a flat cold dark matter model, we find a 68% credible interval of $0.76 \le S_8 \le 0.81$. This result is consistent with the HSC-Y3 cosmic shear analyses (Dalal et al. 2023, Li et al. 2023) but is $\sim 25$% tighter. We also find that the measured B-mode power spectra are consistent with zero. We also perform a performance test using mock catalogs that mimic the HSC-Y3 data to validate our photo-3x2-pt analysis. Through Bayesian parameter inference of mock data, we verify that unbiased estimates can be obtained for the key cosmological and nuisance parameters, including $S_8$, intrinsic alignment model parameters, galaxy clustering bias, and shift parameters of the source redshift distributions.
papers.comments: 20 pages, 23 figures, accepted for PASJ, comments welcome

papers.title: Environmental Noise Challenges for the Einstein Telescope - A Review
papers.abstract: Einstein Telescope (ET) will be a next-generation ground based interferometric gravitational-wave detector designed to explore the Universe to an unprecedented depth and detail. With its 10-15 km long arms, underground infrastructure, and advanced cryogenic technologies to suppress thermal noise, ET aims at achieving a sensitivity up to eight orders of magnitude better than current detectors such as Virgo, LIGO, and KAGRA. The coverage of the low-frequency band, starting at 2 Hz, will enable the observation of earlier inspiral phases of compact binary coalescences, enhancing early-warning capabilities and improving multi-messenger follow-up. However, this increased sensitivity also implies a higher susceptibility to environmental disturbances, particularly in the 2-10 Hz range where anthropogenic, seismic and infrastructural noise noise are most relevant. Therefore, understanding and mitigating environmental contributions are essential to fully exploit the scientific potential of ET. This chapter reviews the ongoing studies on environmental noise for ET, summarizes the main challenges related to site characterization and infrastructure design and outlines the strategies currently under development to ensure optimal detector performance.

papers.title: Static multipolar Einstein-vector-Gauss-Bonnet black holes
papers.abstract: We construct and analyze static multipolar black holes in Einstein-vector-Gauss-Bonnet theory with a quadratic coupling function. The vectorized solutions bifurcate from the Schwarzschild black hole at discrete values of the Gauss-Bonnet coupling, obtained from a perturbative eigenvalue problem on the Schwarzschild background and labelled by the angular multipole number $\ell$. We restrict to the fundamental radial branches. The electric sector contains the known spherically symmetric $\ell=0$ branch as well as axisymmetric branches with $\ell>0$. These electric branches extend to larger values of the coupling. The magnetic sector features a sequence of axisymmetric branches, including the previously found magnetic dipole branch at $\ell=0$. The magnetic branches instead exist only on finite intervals of the coupling, ending at critical solutions. Away from the bifurcation point, nonlinearities generate additional multipoles, but even-$\ell$ and odd-$\ell$ moments remain separated.
papers.comments: 15 pages, 4 figures, final version published in Phys. Lett. B

papers.title: Energy Partitioning in Dust-catalyzed $\mathrm{H_2}$ and HD Formation Revealed by Molecular Simulations Considering Nuclear Quantum Effects
papers.abstract: Molecular hydrogen formation on interstellar dust grains is a key surface process, but the partitioning of recombination energy between the substrate and the nascent molecule remains poorly understood. Here, we use ring-polymer molecular dynamics (RPMD) with a machine-learning force field to investigate energy partitioning during H2 and HD formation on graphene at T=25 K, 50 K and 100 K, focusing on the chemisorbed-H recombination pathway previously identified as the dominant low-temperature channel on bare graphitic surfaces when nuclear quantum effects are included. The desorbing molecule retains approximately 84-87% of the effective released energy, with only weak variation across the three velocity-initialization temperatures under the present sampling protocol. Within the retained molecular energy, rovibrational motion dominates at 25 K, whereas center-of-mass translation becomes increasingly important at 100 K. H2 and HD show similar total energy retention, with modest isotope-dependent differences in their internal partitioning. The effective joint rovibrational distributions show a modest positive association between vibrational and rotational excitation. Purely radiative cascade calculations in the optically thin, collision-free limit yield formation-pumping spectra at all three temperatures. From 25 to 100 K, the rovibrational fraction of the emitted energy decreases from approximately 43% to 28% for H2 and from 41% to 28% for HD, while the strongest lines remain in similar wavelength regions. These results provide an energy-resolved microscopic picture of surface-mediated energy redistribution and formation pumping in H2/HD formation on graphene.
papers.comments: 24 pages, 10 figures. Revised following peer review; accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal

papers.title: Improved constraints on the Milky Way potential using the M68 stream and DESI spectroscopic data
papers.abstract: We present a selection of stars belonging to the stellar stream of the M68 (NGC 4590) globular cluster, also known as Fjörm. This star selection is an improvement on previous ones that used only Gaia data, as it incorporates spectroscopic measurements from the DESI survey and photometric data from the DESI Legacy Surveys. The selection contains 96 stars, each with five phase-space parameters from Gaia-DR3 and radial velocity from DESI, covering the entire observed section of the stream. This constitutes the largest selection of M68 stream stars with measured radial velocities to date. The observed stream is wider than expected from N-body simulations, and the stars farthest from the centre of the stream appear to be correlated in radial velocity space. This suggests that these stars cannot have been stripped from the cluster in a static axisymmetric potential. By modelling a mock sample of stream stars created using an N-body simulation, we found that we could reliably constrain the disc mass $M_{\rm d}$ and the dark matter halo axis ratio $q_{\rm h}$ of the Milky Way. This is because the stream flows close to and almost parallel to the disc. Using the 44 stars that are consistent with having been stripped from the cluster, combined with measurements of the Milky Way's rotation curve, we constrain the Galactic potential, obtaining $M_{\rm d} = 5.34 \pm 0.57 \times 10^{10}$ M$_{\rm sun}$ and an oblate halo of $q_{\rm h} = 0.83^{+0.06}_{-0.05}$. Additionally, by fitting the stream track, we estimate the Heliocentric distance of M68 to be $r=10.55\pm0.09$ kpc.

papers.title: A posteriori correction of Gaia CRF proper motions using conditional probability and zero-parallax prior
papers.abstract: The formal precision of Gaia CRF proper motions, and in principle positions, can be statistically improved by introducing conditional probability based on the zero-parallax prior for these extremely distant sources. The method developed in this study produces statistically conditioned proper-motion estimates under the assumed per-source Gaussian covariance model. It is demonstrated that thus corrected proper motion vectors of 1.2 million CRF objects in Gaia DR3 show a tighter distribution around zero and a general reduction in the rate of outliers by approximately 15\%. A general vector spherical harmonic fit to degree 4 is produced with the corrected data for a filtered subset of CRF quasars with redshifts between 1 and 1.5. This application, predicated on the unknown stochastic component of the global parallax field, shows a 3-sigma change in the estimated magnitude of the Galactocentric acceleration of the solar system barycenter, quantifying the sensitivity of this fundamental determination to the proposed conditioning of proper motions.
papers.comments: Published in PASP 138:104509, October 2026, DOI https://doi.org/10.1088/1538-3873/aea7da

papers.title: Super-Eddington Accretion and Early-Stage Feedback in Ton S180
papers.abstract: Narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1) galaxies are key laboratories for studying rapid supermassive black hole (SMBH) growth and active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback at high accretion rates. We investigate the nearby NLSy1 Ton S180 with VLT-MUSE optical integral field spectroscopy to connect its nuclear accretion properties with the spatially resolved ionized gas and host-galaxy kinematics. We modeled the unresolved nuclear spectrum and applied a custom point spread function subtraction to recover the host-galaxy emission on kiloparsec scales. The nuclear spectrum requires a complex permitted-line decomposition and a blueshifted [O III] outflow component. Single-epoch estimators and the stellar velocity dispersion imply black hole masses in the range $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot) = 6.5 - 7.7$. Combined with the observed luminosity, this implies a dimensionless mass accretion rate of $\dot{M} / \dot{M}_{\rm Edd} = 4.1 - 980$, confirming the extreme accretion regime. The host galaxy shows a circumnuclear ring, an inner elongated structure consistent with a bar, and rotation-dominated gas and stellar kinematics. Simple inflow models do not significantly better reproduce the observed velocity field. We detect a resolved ionized outflow extending about 2 kpc west of the nucleus, with mildly blueshifted velocities (with a maximum of $v_{\rm max} \sim 340$ km s$^{-1}$). Its mass outflow rate is only $\sim 4.2 \times 10^{-4}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, whereas the unresolved nuclear outflow reaches $v_{\rm max} \sim 1140$ km s$^{-1}$ and $\dot{M}_{\rm out} > 1.5\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. This contrast may reflect either weak ionized coupling from nuclear to galactic scales or different episodes of AGN activity over time. These results show that Ton S180 is undergoing rapid SMBH growth, while the observed ionized outflow remains confined to the inner few kiloparsecs and is weak on host-galaxy scales.
papers.comments: 15 pages (main text), 8 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A (1 September 2026)

papers.title: Conformally Coupled Scalar- Field Dark Energy: Cosmological Dynamics with Early- and Late- Measurements
papers.abstract:
In this work, the cosmology of the conformal interacting dark energy model is investigated by introducing a scalar field representing dark energy (DE) coupled to dark matter (DM) via a conformal transformation. This coupling yields a class of scalar+tensor theories; the interaction term ${Q}$, which indicates the flow of energy between the dark sectors, is proportional to the trace of the energy-momentum tensor of the DM fluid, $T^{\mathrm{DM}}_{\mu
u}$, as ${Q}= rac{C'(\phi)}{2C(\phi)}g^{\mu
u}T^{\mathrm{DM}}_{\mu
u}$, where $C(\phi)$ is the conformal function of a scalar potential (coupling) field. We assume the power-law parametrization $C(\phi)\propto (1+\phi)^m$, with $m$ as the coupling parameter, and determine the direction and magnitude of energy flow between the DM and DE scalar-field components. We model DE in three scenarios: conformally interacting dark energy (CIDE) coupled to a scalar field, uncoupled scalar+field DE (UCSFDE), and standard $ \Lambda$CDM models. We confront these models with cosmological measurements to test the viability of CIDE and UCSFED against $\Lambda$CDM and constrain them using a combination of early and late time data, namely: Cosmic Microwave Background measurements from Planck 2018 Legacy (	exttt{CMB}); Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) data from the Dark Energy Survey (	exttt{ DESI DR2 DR2 BAO}); and Supernova Type Ia distance compilations (	exttt{PantheonPlus, PantheonPlus + SH0ES, Union3}, and 	exttt{DES+Dovekie}). We perform parameter inference with Monte Carlo Markov Chain (	exttt{MCMC}) simulations using 	exttt{COBAYA} and a modified 	exttt{CLASS} ...

papers.title: Theoretical Aspects of Direct Waves in Kerr Black Holes: Pole-Splitting Method for Ringdown Analysis
papers.abstract: We develop a theoretical description of direct waves (DWs) from a particle plunging into a Kerr black hole in the extreme-mass-ratio regime. A DW is characterized by a source-driven complex frequency $\omega_{\rm G}$ that reflects the particle's orbital motion, including motion inside the ergoregion. Hence, it is expected to be a probe of rich structures of Kerr black holes. We show that the contribution of the quasinormal-mode (QNM) pole sector to the DW is part of dynamical QNM excitation. We also show that the apparent horizon-mode poles cancel at every order of a consistent near-horizon expansion of the trajectory, homogeneous radial solution, and complete point-particle source. This result assumes that the point particle follows a geodesic near the horizon and leaves open the possibility of a transient DW while the particle passes near the ergosurface or the vicinity of the potential barrier. To investigate this possibility in simulated plunge waveforms, we develop a pole-splitting method that decomposes the transfer function into QNM-pole and non-pole parts. The resulting waveform decomposition avoids the frequency-dependent time shift (group delay) introduced by the QNM filtering. For quasi-circular plunges into moderately and rapidly rotating Kerr black holes, the frequency and decay rate of the non-pole waveform show qualitative agreement with our theoretical prediction over finite time intervals. These results support the potential use of DWs as probes of the ergoregion and gravitational redshift effect around black holes.
papers.comments: 20 pages, 8 figures. v2: Sec. II F and all related discussion have been removed because the analysis in that section was incorrect. The main results and conclusions are unaffected. v3: Added Sec. II F on the cancellation of horizon-mode poles to all orders in the near-horizon expansion and its relation to direct waves

papers.title: Tangled $τ$: Planck CMB Constraints on Flash Reionization
papers.abstract: Recent cosmological tensions have renewed interest in the role of reionization in parameter inference, and flash reionization has been proposed as a transient high-redshift ionization episode that can increase the Thomson optical depth while remaining compatible with CMB polarization data. In this work, we present the first Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis of the flash reionization model fit to Planck cosmic microwave background temperature, polarization, and lensing data. We perform this analysis using Planck PR4 data in $\Lambda$CDM with flash reionization. We find that CMB data allow a wide range for the redshift of the flash, $z_{\rm flash}$, but with constraints that are tightly correlated with the peak ionization fraction $x_{\rm flash}$. We find constraints $x_{\rm flash}=0.24 ^{+0.13} _{-0.07}$ and $x_{\rm flash}= 0.15 ^{+0.07} _{ - 0.05}$ for the benchmark flash reionization scenarios with fixed $z_{\rm flash}=20$ and $25$ respectively. The standard $\Lambda$CDM parameters do not exhibit any significant shifts, and in particular, the total optical depth to reionization is not appreciably changed, with $\tau=0.061 \pm 0.007$ in flash reionization as compared to $\tau=0.059\pm 0.006$ in the standard tanh parametrization. We repeat this analysis for Planck PR3 data in place of PR4, and find that the mild preference for a flash is replaced by 95% CL upper bounds, given by $x_{\rm flash}<0.28$ and $x_{\rm flash}<0.18$ for $z_{\rm flash}=20$ and $25$, respectively, from Planck PR3 data.

papers.title: Dark matter haloes from dwarf to massive galaxies: no systematic inner-density tension with ΛCDM hydrodynamical simulations
papers.abstract: Two of the most prominent small-scale challenges to the cold dark matter (CDM) paradigm are the cusp-core and diversity-of-rotation-curves problems. The former concerns the shallow inner DM density profiles inferred for many galaxies compared with the cusps predicted by collisionless CDM, while the latter concerns the wider range of inner DM densities and rotation curve shapes inferred observationally than hydrodynamical simulations traditionally reproduce. Robust observational constraints on DM core sizes and halo densities are therefore essential for testing both the nature of DM and the impact of galaxy formation processes. We analyse the inner DM distribution of a curated sample of 48 gas-rich galaxies and 8 Milky Way gas-poor satellites, spanning 6 orders of magnitude in $M_\ast$. We find substantial scatter in DM core sizes and degrees of coreness, with both cuspy and cored haloes occurring over a broad $M_\ast$ range. The cores are energetically consistent with stellar feedback, requiring modest supernova energy coupling efficiencies of order $0.1-1\%$. Comparisons with the NIHAO, FIRE-2, and EDGE simulations reveal broad agreement in the inner DM densities and logarithmic slopes of observed and simulated galaxies. The main residual differences concern the steep slopes of some massive simulated galaxies and differences in SHMRs. Using a rotation-curve diversity diagnostic from previous work, we find that extreme discrepancies with simulations are absent from our curated sample and largely attributable to uncertain kinematics or baryonic mass distributions. Within the scope of our analysis, we find no evidence of a systematic inner-density tension between our galaxy sample and current $\Lambda$CDM hydrodynamical simulations. Together with the modest energetic requirements for core formation, this substantially alleviates the cusp-core and diversity-of-rotation-curves problems.

papers.title: Gravity-Informed Neural Networks for Post-Newtonian Binary Dynamics
papers.abstract: We introduce a gravity-informed neural-network (GravINNs) framework for learning post-Newtonian binary orbital dynamics. The method incorporates the equations of motion directly into the training phase and is developed at three complementary levels. First, we construct single-orbit surrogates for conservative post-Newtonian dynamics and assess their accuracy across different orbital configurations. We then extend the approach to a parametric model spanning a four-dimensional parameter space defined by the initial separation, radial and tangential momenta, and symmetric mass ratio, allowing a single trained network to represent entire families of orbits and replace repeated numerical integrations. Finally, we consider dissipative dynamics by including the leading radiation-reaction contribution at $2.5$PN order. In this regime, the network reproduces the orbital evolution and the associated secular energy loss, starting from a conservative 2PN warm start and without using dissipative reference trajectories in the training. These results show that physics-informed neural-networks (PINNs) can provide accurate and flexible representations of both conservative and dissipative post-Newtonian dynamics. The complete implementation and the models used in this work are publicly available through the \texttt{GravINNs} repository.
papers.comments: 21 pages, 6 figures. Code available at: this https URL

papers.title: Mass inflation or scalaron rigidity: Cauchy horizons in metric f(R)
papers.abstract: We develop a double-null framework for Cauchy-horizon dynamics in metric $f(R)$ gravity that separates ordinary mass inflation from scalaron cancellation and genuine escape from the blueshift instability. Starting from the exact spherical Hawking-mass transport equation, we show that a regular nondegenerate Cauchy horizon undergoes mass inflation whenever the effective longitudinal source is eventually nonnegative, uniformly dominates the mixed channel, and has a divergent blueshift-weighted integral. Hence bounded mass requires sufficiently strong blueshift-integrable suppression of this source or an independent competing channel. We then analyze the weaker branch in which the scalaron cancels only the leading Price-tail contribution. Under non-cancelling transverse and trace asymptotics, this forces $|R|\to\infty$ and an asymptotically linear high-curvature theory, $f(R)/R\to F_->0$, where $F_-\equiv\lim_{v\to\infty}f_R$. The curvature coefficient is fixed explicitly by the transverse asymptotics. For regular model classes with a finite high-curvature $f_{RR}$ limit one obtains $f_{RR}\to0$. More sharply, every eventually viable branch with $f_{RR}>0$ is forced to $R\to-\infty$ and $\Lambda_\infty>-1$; the standard scalaron mass parameter then diverges, while an additional differentiable rate condition yields $m_{\rm sc}^2\sim F/(3f_{RR})\to+\infty$. In the Einstein frame the scalaron null kinetic contribution is nonnegative, so the Jordan-frame cancellation cannot be interpreted as negative scalaron null energy. The result is a local rigidity classification rather than a global theorem of strong cosmic censorship.

papers.title: A sub-100 pc view at z~5 of a multiply imaged massive quiescent galaxy
papers.abstract: James Webb Space Telescope surveys reveal many rapidly assembled galaxies in the first billion years. Simulations struggle to reproduce their rapid star formation and abrupt cessation, known as quenching. Testing these models is difficult because high-redshift galaxies are compact and appear unresolved. We present VENUS-CLJ0152-QG1, a massive post-starburst galaxy at redshift 5.18. A foreground cluster lenses it into three images, yielding a physical resolution of about 70 parsecs, enough to probe quenching processes on sub-kiloparsec scales. We find a half-light radius twice as large as expected, a central stellar mass density three times lower than field analogs, and off-center ionized gas emission. These features suggest it quenched without compaction or an obvious active galactic nucleus, a departure from unlensed high-redshift galaxies that lensing makes visible.
papers.comments: 26 pages, 6 Figures, 1 Table. Submitted to Science

papers.title: Emergent Scaling Symmetry and Universal Interior Criticality of Scalarized Black Holes
papers.abstract: The interiors of spontaneously scalarized charged black holes exhibit a tower of universality classes, including the previously reported $1/2$ scaling. We show that their near-critical collapse is governed by an emergent scaling symmetry at the would-be Cauchy horizon. This symmetry renders the interior dynamics autonomous, model-independent, and exactly integrable, realizing first-kind self-similarity rather than Choptuik-type second-kind criticality. It also yields a ``seesaw amplification'': an arbitrarily small exterior hair produces an arbitrarily large interior response. The amplification obeys an amplitude identity relating three independently measurable quantities. The singularity exponent equals the critical exponent of the exterior scalar charge. These relations connect the exterior phase transition to the approach to the interior singularity through the scaling dynamics near the would-be Cauchy horizon.

papers.title: Teleparallel Renormalization of Gravitational Action
papers.abstract: We study the gravitational action in the teleparallel equivalent of general relativity, where the spin connection contributes to the action through a surface term and, when chosen appropriately, regularizes the action by effectively playing the role of a counterterm. We resolve several apparent ambiguities in this procedure using the Schwarzschild spacetime as an example. We show that the apparent discrepancy between bulk and quasilocal actions originates from contributions associated with spacetime singularities, and that the quasilocal action agrees with the standard results obtained in general relativity. We further clarify the role of the tetrad choice in determining the corresponding spin connection, showing that the proper diagonal and canonical frames give the same Euclidean action, while only the proper diagonal frame reproduces the expected Lorentzian action on the Wheeler--DeWitt patch. Finally, we establish the uniqueness of the regularization scheme and show that imposing an appropriate fall-off behavior of the torsion tensor removes the remaining ambiguity and fixes the Euclidean action uniquely.

papers.title: Neutrino Direct Simulation Monte Carlo: Accurate modeling of out-of-equilibrium decaying cosmological relics
papers.abstract:
We consider nonstandard cosmologies in which decaying relics inject energy at MeV temperatures, driving neutrinos out of equilibrium. The subsequent neutrino evolution shapes predictions for the cosmic radiation density and primordial light element abundances. Earlier work introduced Neutrino Direct Simulation Monte Carlo ($
u$DSMC), which describes neutrino transport through Monte Carlo sampling of particle interactions. Here, we extend this method by jointly evolving the relic population, neutrino spectra, electromagnetic plasma, and cosmic expansion, and coupling this evolution to Big Bang nucleosynthesis. The framework includes direct and inverse decays of the relic, neutrino flavor conversion, quantum statistics, and pion production by energetic neutrinos. To reveal the physical impact of these effects and independently test $
u$DSMC, we compare several approaches to neutrino evolution across a range of nonstandard cosmological scenarios. We find excellent agreement with independent solutions of quantum kinetic or quasi-classical Boltzmann equations. Compared with these calculations, $
u$DSMC includes a broader range of physical processes and is substantially faster for strongly nonthermal neutrino populations. This makes broad, robust parameter scans for nonstandard cosmologies practical. We show that when departures from thermal equilibrium are large, approximations that average over neutrino momenta can give qualitatively incorrect predictions, including the wrong sign of the change in the effective number of neutrino species and substantially incorrect primordial nuclear abundances. We conclude that the extended $
u$DSMC framework enables reliable cosmological tests of new physics by following neutrino thermalization and its observable consequences.

papers.title: Two-horizon sector thermodynamics and NUT bi-hair in Kerr-Newman-NUT spacetimes
papers.abstract: First law consistency alone does not determine the black hole state space of NUT-charged spacetimes, because several inequivalent macroscopic formulations can yield consistent thermodynamics. We develop a two-horizon sector diagnostic for the electrically charged Kerr-Newman-NUT family by organizing the inner- and outer-horizon entropies and inverse temperatures into sum ($\Sigma$) and difference ($\Delta$) sectors. The charged rotating geometry gives a more stringent test of the uncharged Taub-NUT sector result, since the mass $M$, ordinary electric charge $Q$, ordinary angular momentum $J$, NUT charge $N$, and the NUT secondary hair $J_N=MN$ all enter the same two-horizon thermodynamics. For the physically anchored minimal homogeneous state spaces defined and tested here, we find a clear sector separation: the $\Sigma$ sector closes with the charge-like variables $Q$ and $N$, whereas the $\Delta$ sector additionally requires the rotation-like variables $J$ and $J_N$. Natural reductions that eliminate either $J_N$ or $N$ fail to reproduce the first law coefficient fixed by the sector temperature, and their associated Bekenstein-Smarr relations do not close with the assigned scaling weights. Within this class, electric charge and ordinary rotation therefore do not absorb the NUT secondary response, and the charged rotating family supports the NUT bi-hair organization: $N$ has a charge-like sector role, while $J_N=MN$ is a rotation-like thermodynamic secondary hair. The latter is defined off shell in the homogeneous equation of state, not as a new metric parameter or asymptotic conserved charge.

papers.title: Revisiting the Duff Argument in Cosmology: From Dimensional Quantities to Cross-Epoch Observables
papers.abstract: The standard Duff-type argument states that the numerical variation of a dimensional constant is unit-dependent when considered in isolation from the physical standards used to compare it, and is therefore not by itself an observable. We ask whether this conclusion is sufficient to determine the observational status of complete relations connecting different cosmological epochs. In a Robertson--Walker spacetime, the cosmological principle and Weyl's postulate fix the homogeneous geometry and fundamental timelike congruence without uniquely fixing the temporal rate along it. The Hamiltonian constraint likewise does not dynamically select that rate. Consequently, Robertson--Walker spacetime admits a family of homogeneous temporal parametrizations. Generalized Cosmological Time retains a specified common member, T_G, related to proper time by d tau = N_G d T_G, with (tau, 1) as the unit-rate special member of the same class. In the minimally extended varying speed of light framework, length--mass--time quantities obey correlated slice-wise scalings chosen to preserve the same local physical laws on every homogeneous hypersurface. These scalings form a unit-rescaling structure, so purely local dimensionless observables are insensitive to N_G. Cross-epoch observables require more than such local scalings. They also require local reference standards, a propagation or comparison map, and, when distinct source populations are compared, a source-equivalence prescription. Cosmological time dilation illustrates this distinction: its interpretation depends on source standardization and residual source evolution. We distinguish the unit dependence of individual dimensional quantities from the observational content of complete cross-epoch relations. The former does not by itself determine the latter.
papers.comments: 17 pages, 1 table, v2: Substantially revised and expanded. Title changed; cross-epoch observability, temporal parametrization, and source-equivalence/source-evolution treatments have been reformulated and clarified. References updated

papers.title: Quantum Love and ringdown near extremality
papers.abstract: In this paper we discuss the quasinormal modes and the tidal responses of a four-dimensional asymptotically flat Reissner-Nordström black hole near extremality and investigate the nontrivial near-horizon quantum corrections of these observables. The near-horizon dynamics of near extremal black holes are generally governed by an effective Schwarzian action coupled to boundary gauge modes. We use this description and couple this effective theory with a massless scalar field outside. Using this setup we compute $2 \to 2$ scattering process of a black hole and a scalar particle. The poles of the scattering amplitude at complex frequencies give us the quasinormal mode spectrum and we recover the predicted zero damped modes near extremality at leading order. Next we evaluate the static Love numbers from the elastic limit of the scattering amplitude. We show that the static Love numbers are non-zero in contrast to the classical expectations. Very close to extremality, the behaviour is analytic, but as the near-extremal energy becomes sufficiently large, we find logarithmic dependence on the energy. This cannot be removed by the choice of renormalisation scheme. Thus near-horizon quantum effects non-trivially change the tidal response of near-extremal black holes.

papers.title: SCALES. I. Bridging Lensed Clump - Giant Clump Scales in Lensed Galaxies at $z=1-4$
papers.abstract: Dense star-forming regions in $z>1$ galaxies, often termed 'clumps', have been studied across two distinct regimes of telescope resolution, each motivating interpretations in tension with the other. In the SCALES series (Star-Forming Clumps As Layered Emergent Structures), we aim to connect star-forming structures across scales, from the $\sim100\,\mathrm{pc}$ clumps in lensed studies to the $\sim\mathrm{kpc}$-scale ''giant'' clumps in unlensed surveys. In this first paper, we present a difference-of-Gaussian (DoG) decomposition that simultaneously models $\approx 50-400\,\mathrm{pc}$ (lensed) clumps and $\sim\mathrm{kpc}$-scale component (the extended component, or EC), which would together constitute the giant clumps seen at lower resolution. Here the EC is treated as a scale-separated local background rather than a physical object, absorbing all light that is not a compact clump. Applying this to 23 moderately lensed ($\mu \approx 2-9$) galaxies at $z_{spec} = 1-4$ to evaluate clump properties (deferring ECs and giant clumps to SCALES-II), we measure a clump stellar mass function slope of $1.88 \pm 0.04$, consistent with the $\approx2$ expected for hierarchical star formation, and with that of $\sim\mathrm{kpc}$-scale clumps in unlensed galaxies. We also show that empirical correlations of clump surface densities and clump-to-host mass ratio with redshift are exaggerated by redshift-dependent detection bias, so $\approx 50-400\,\mathrm{pc}$ clumps are largely co-similar across our range ($z = 1-4$). Finally, combining clump mass, size and age estimates with literature gas-dispersion measurements at similar scales, we argue that $\sim100\,\mathrm{pc}$ clumps are themselves composed of star-cluster-like sub-components at much smaller scales.
papers.comments: Submitted to ApJ; 36 pages, 21 figures. Companion paper (this http URL.) appears on arXiv simultaneously

papers.title: SCALES. II. The Internal Composition of Giant Star-Forming Clumps at $z = 1 - 4$
papers.abstract: Star-forming structures of scale $\sim0.5-1\,\mathrm{kpc}$, dubbed 'giant' clumps, are routinely detected in unlensed surveys of $z > 1$ galaxies. Explaining them requires characterizing their internal structure. In this work, part of the Star-Forming Clumps As Layered Emergent Structures (SCALES) series, we hence ask: What is inside a giant clump? We analyze 23 lensed galaxies at $z=1-4$ with JWST/NIRCam using a difference-of-Gaussian decomposition to model (lensed) clumps at $\approx 50-400\,\mathrm{pc}$ scales, and the surrounding extended component (EC) at giant clump scales. Associating clumps to ECs, we identify 72 giant clumps. We find the constituent clumps above our mass completeness limit ($10^{7.1}\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$) in a giant clump to be consistent with random sampling of the clump stellar mass function (CSMF), hence holding no information about their host. This agrees qualitatively with both prevailing scenarios for giant clumps: (I) long-lived structures with constantly renewed constituents, and (II) blended random clump associations. As most models lack predictions for their internal mass distribution, our observations provide an empirical constraint. Finally, the CSMF follows a power law of slope $1.88\pm0.04$ above a break at $\sim10^{7.5}\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, close to our completeness limit. The giant clumps follow a consistent slope ($1.95\pm0.15$), giving the same scale-free mass function slope at (lensed) clump and giant clump scales. Within giant clumps, both the EC mass, if made up of undetected clumps, and the mass share of the most massive clump are consistent with the CSMF slope continuing down to $\approx10^{5.5}-10^{6}\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, while the latter rejects an extension below $10^{5}\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$.
papers.comments: Submitted to ApJ; 21 pages, 13 figures. Companion paper (SCALES-I) appears on arXiv simultaneously

papers.title: Wald entropy and Wen-Zee type gauge-curvature coupling in 2+1-dimensional gravity
papers.abstract: The Wen-Zee term is a mixed gauge-curvature coupling in the topological Chern-Simons description of a quantum Hall fluid, encoding the electric charge bound to spatial curvature. We investigate a Lorentz-covariant generalization of this coupling, expanding its scope to black-hole spacetimes and determine its contribution to horizon entropy. Such a coupling arises naturally in three-dimensional Chern-Simons gravity based on the Maxwell algebra. We show that its Wald entropy contribution is a horizon boost charge, given by a loop integral of the additional gauge field projected along the tangent to the bifurcation circle. This contribution can be nonzero even when the mixed term vanishes on shell. We show that the integral admits an Abelian holonomy interpretation when the projection direction is covariantly constant. We evaluate the charge on a flat cosmological solution and, using smooth horizon fields and a specified thermal ensemble, on an AdS-Lorentz black hole. These results connect the geometric response familiar from quantum Hall physics to gravitational horizon thermodynamics.
papers.comments: 39 pages, v2: revised Appendix D, minor corrections and consistent spelling, added citations

papers.title: Dyonic Simpson Visser black-bounce spacetime surrounded by an exotic Einstein cluster in general relativity
papers.abstract: In this work, we present the Simpson-Visser black-bounce (SV-BB) spacetime with both electric and magnetic charges (the dyonic SV-BB) as an exact solution of general relativity coupled to Maxwell electrodynamics and an anisotropic fluid with vanishing radial pressure. We assume the anisotropic fluid represents an Einstein cluster, which consists of a dense system of particles moving in circular orbits that generate only tangential pressure and zero radial pressure. We show that the electromagnetic SV-BB metric, which provides a regular black hole spacetime, can be obtained as an exact solution to the Einstein field equations sourced by a combination of an Einstein cluster (which is responsible for providing the exotic matter required to keep a black-bounce throat open) and an electromagnetic field in the framework of Maxwell electrodynamics.
papers.comments: 18 pages. Revised in response to referee comments

papers.title: Cosmic Birefringence from Large Lepton Asymmetry
papers.abstract: Cosmic birefringence, the rotation of the polarization plane of cosmic microwave background (CMB) photons, provides an intriguing probe of physics beyond the Standard Model. In this paper, we investigate a vector Chern-Simons coupling between the neutrino current and photons as a possible origin of isotropic cosmic birefringence. Firstly, we perform the first analysis of anisotropic cosmic birefringence induced by the neutrino current. We find that the anisotropic signal sourced by lepton-number isocurvature fluctuations can be important on large scales, whereas on small scales, the anisotropic signal induced by gravitational effects becomes dominant comparing with the axion-like particle (ALP) scenario. Secondly, we show that a large lepton asymmetry generated through the Affleck-Dine mechanism can successfully account for the observed isotropic birefringence, and discuss its possible connection to the recently reported low helium-4 abundances in Subaru EMPRESS and Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT).

papers.title: Redundant Records of the Past: Unifying Quantum Darwinism and Decoherent Histories
papers.abstract: There exist two different paradigms for records in isolated quantum systems: decoherent histories (which determines which past events leave formal records) and quantum Darwinism (which determines which current events get redundantly recorded). Neither one implies the other, and connections between the two are scarcely investigated. We unify quantum Darwinism and decoherent histories based on the insight that only redundant records about past events matter. The resulting framework of past redundancy encompasses quantum Darwinism when applied to events at the current time, and it implies the probability sum rule or decoherence of histories. The Bhattacharyya coefficient (or fidelity) plays an important role to establish this connection. Importantly, various examples show that past redundancy is a more widespread phenomenon than the fine-tuned models necessary for quantum Darwinism suggest. We thus arrive at a richer picture in which redundancy can be caused by mechanisms different from quantum Darwinism (such as macroevents or cascade structures), which emphasizes that redundancy is necessary but not sufficient for objectivity, and which, overall, allows to realistically investigate the question: how generic is redundancy in nature?
papers.comments: Improved clarity and a new result (redundancy implies classicality). One more page. Comments from v1 still apply

papers.title: Widespread steep X-ray spectra of luminous $z=5.85-7.64$ quasars and their implications for future X-ray surveys
papers.abstract: Luminous quasars (QSOs) at the Epoch of Reionization (EoR, $z\gtrsim6$) host billion-solar-mass black holes assembled within the first Gyr of cosmic time. Their X-ray emission probes the innermost accreting regions and constrains the physical state of the corona during early supermassive black hole (SMBH) growth. Previous results from the HYPerluminous quasars at the Epoch of ReionizatION (HYPERION) sample of $z \gtrsim 6$ QSOs, powered by the most rapidly accreted SMBHs, suggested a link between X-ray spectral slope and long-term growth efficiency. We test whether the steep X-ray spectra of luminous z>6 QSOs are a general property of early SMBH growth or a peculiarity of the most efficiently grown SMBHs, using a sample extended mainly to the lowest growth efficiencies. We analysed the largest and most X-ray sensitive sample of 28 luminous QSOs at $z = 5.85-7.64$ (26 used in the correlation analysis), combining HYPERION targets, luminous non-HYPERION sources, and QSOs powered by moderately accreting SMBHs newly observed in our XMM-Newton Large Programme. We re-derived black hole masses and growth indicators for the entire sample homogeneously, incorporating the latest JWST-based spectroscopic measurements to ensure the most consistent and high-quality characterization across all targets. We found no statistically significant correlation between coronal spectral parameters and BH growth indicators: luminous $z \gtrsim 6$ QSOs systematically show steep X-ray continua, with high photon indices and/or low high-energy cutoffs, consistent with cold coronae, possibly linked to rapid accretion. Finally, if steep X-ray slopes are common among early AGN, they may significantly reduce count rates, at fixed intrinsic luminosity, in future surveys of the EoR, affecting the detectability of steep-spectrum X-ray sources and thus the census of the early AGN population.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in A&A after minor revisions

papers.title: Reconstruction of Black Hole Islands from Hawking Radiation via the Algebraic Petz Map
papers.abstract: The island proposal guarantees a unitary Page curve for evaporating black holes, implying that operators deep behind the horizon must be fully reconstructable from asymptotic Hawking radiation. However, because the interior is causally disconnected and highly dynamical, standard entanglement wedge reconstruction methods, relying on global isometries or continuous modular flow, fail to provide this mapping. We resolve this by constructing a protocol for island reconstruction using the algebraic Petz map. By using modular theory, we reflect island operators into the accessible complement, transport them to the boundary, and map them into the radiation algebra. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this purely algebraic derivation naturally yields the structure of Papadodimas-Raju mirror operators. This framework provides a rigorous operational dictionary for the island formula, proving that information trapped inside a black hole can be decoded.
papers.comments: v2: Typos corrected, references added, comments added to Sections II and III, and acknowledgments updated

papers.title: TDCOSMO 2026: A 3% measurement of the Hubble constant from strong lensing and stellar kinematics
papers.abstract: We present cosmological constraints from 11 strongly lensed quasars with measured time delays (hereafter, the TDCOSMO-2026 sample). In addition to expanding the sample, we improve many aspects of our blind analysis with respect to our 2025 analysis. Among other improvements, spatially resolved kinematics are available for nine systems, including six with JWST-NIRSpec, compared to one in 2025; for three lens models, JWST-NIRCam images now replace HST; axisymmetric dynamical modeling is applied directly to the spatially resolved data, instead of an axisymmetric correction factor applied to spherical models; and the line-of-sight convergence is now based on the Euclid Flagship simulations instead of the Millennium Simulation. Our baseline and primary result is based on the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, in combination with a prior on $\Omega_{\rm m}$ from the DES-Dovekie supernova sample. In the flat $\Lambda$ cold dark matter ($\Lambda$CDM) cosmology, we find $H_0=71.1^{+2.4}_{-2.3}$ km.s$^{-1}$.Mpc$^{-1}$, a 3.3% uncertainty that accounts for the mass-sheet degeneracy. The SLACS and SL2S samples are in excellent agreement with the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, improving the precision on $H_0$ in flat $\Lambda$CDM to 3.0%. Using the DESI-DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) likelihood instead of DES-Dovekie yields fully consistent results. We also present constraints in the open $\Lambda$CDM, $w$CDM, $w_0w_a$CDM, and $w_{\phi}$CDM cosmologies; the TDCOSMO $H_0$ inference is robust and consistent across all of them. The combination of the TDCOSMO+SLACS+SL2S likelihood with those from DESI-DR2 and DES-Dovekie disfavors $w=-1$ at the $2.3$-$2.5\sigma$ level in all three dark energy extensions that we tested. We find, e.g., $w_0=-0.88^{+0.04}_{-0.05}$ in $w_{\phi}$CDM and $w_0 = -0.85^{+0.07}_{-0.06}$ in $w_0w_a$CDM, while $w_a = -0.48^{+0.46}_{-0.44}$ remains consistent with zero.
papers.comments: Submitted to Physical Review D (PRD). Summary of the results are presented in arXiv:2610.14881. The data and likelihoods will be made publicly available upon acceptance

papers.title: TDCOSMO 2026: new insights on the Hubble tension from strong lensing time delays
papers.abstract: We discuss the measurement of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) in flat $\Lambda$ cold dark matter cosmology based on the blind hierarchical analysis of 11 multiply-imaged quasars (hereafter the TDCOSMO-2026 sample) and described in greater detail in a companion paper. In addition to the time delays, we use lens models based on high-resolution imaging from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), analyzed jointly with axisymmetric dynamical models based on JWST-NIRSpec, VLT-MUSE, and Keck-KCWI spectroscopy. Our primary result $H_0=71.1^{+2.4}_{-2.3}$ km.s$^{-1}$.Mpc$^{-1}$ is based on the TDCOSMO-2026 sample, in combination with $\Omega_{\rm m}$ constraints from the DES-Dovekie supernova (SN) dataset. Our 3% precision accounts for the mass-sheet degeneracy. Importantly, our measurement is independent of the local distance ladder (LDL). Among individual late-universe probes, only the traditional LDL is more precise. We discuss our result in the context of the Hubble tension, the difference between $H_0$ measured in the late universe and the prediction based on early-universe probes such as the cosmic microwave background (CMB). We construct combinations of independent late-universe probes and show that the tension with the Planck CMB prediction is robust to excluding any one of the methods based on Type-Ia Supernovae, Cepheids, or the Tip of the Red Giant Branch. For example, we construct a 'no-SN' $H_0$ measurement, by replacing the DES-Dovekie constraint on $\Omega_{\rm m}$ with that from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations, and then combining TDCOSMO-2026 with independent non-SN late-universe probes. This 'no-SN' late-universe probe is in 3.7$\sigma$ tension with Planck. Even after completely excluding the LDL, the tension with Planck persists at the 2.7$\sigma$ level.
papers.comments: Submitted to PRL. 11 pages, 3 figures. Detailed analysis presented in arXiv:2610.14781

papers.title: GroArnold: A Framework for Constructing Action-based Models for Triaxial Galaxies and Dark Matter Halos
papers.abstract: Action-based distribution functions $f(\mathbf{J})$ provide a powerful description of stellar systems. Consequently, the construction of physically accurate and dynamically stable $f(\mathbf{J})$ for galactic components has emerged as a key challenge in the field. In this study, we present GroArnold, a computational framework designed to construct analytical $f(\mathbf{J})$ expressions for axisymmetric and triaxial galaxies and dark matter halos. The framework integrates modules for $N$-body initial condition generation, $N$-body simulation, angle--action variable estimation, and distribution-function fitting into a unified workflow. It supports a wide range of density profiles and kinematic properties, and is uniquely designed to generate stable $N$-body models for user-specified galactic systems, with the aim of obtaining an $f(\mathbf{J})$ that approximates a dynamically stable and physically consistent state. To this end, we extend the triaxial Stäckel Fudge method of the TACT code, implemented in our Nbody-TACT module, to enable action estimation directly from $N$-body gravitational potentials. GroArnold provides a robust and flexible tool for deriving numerically empirical, explicitly analytical distribution functions for user-specified galaxies or halos, thereby facilitating a wide range of practical $f(\mathbf{J})$-based modeling applications. In addition, it serves as a powerful tool for investigating the dynamics of realistic triaxial galaxies and halos beyond the scope of traditional spherical or axisymmetric models. We assessed the accuracy of the output $f(\mathbf{J})$ by comparing its predicted spatial and velocity distributions with those of the input $N$-body snapshot, and confirmed that it provides a reasonably accurate representation of the input. The code is modular, publicly available, and designed to support future extensions and adaptations.
papers.comments: Our key results: see the logic flow of the code in Fig. 1; see the universal $f(J)$ function in Eq. (13) and its fitting demonstration in Fig. 8

papers.title: Magnetically Charged Black Holes from Grand Unified Theory
papers.abstract: Grand Unified models of particle physics inevitably give rise to magnetic monopoles. Often the model will also contain a weakly broken discrete symmetry that leads to the formation of biased domain walls that survive for a limited period in cosmology. For a range of the discrete symmetry breaking parameter, domain walls can collapse to form magnetically charged extremal black holes lighter than $\simeq 1\, {\rm kg}$ but these are not expected to survive until the present epoch due to Hawking evaporation and Schwinger pair production of monopoles. If the parameter is smaller still, the black holes may be astrophysical, with mass greater than $10^{15}\, {\rm g}$ and with sub-extremal magnetic charge: $Q \simeq 10^8$ (for our canonical choice of parameters). The cosmological energy density in residual magnetic monopoles depends on the discrete symmetry breaking parameter and for sufficiently small values of the parameter, the magnetic monopole density can satisfy all observational constraints.
papers.comments: 9 pages, 2 figures, added comment and reference on Landau levels

papers.title: Group averaging and the geometry of physical quantum states: from normalizable solutions to solvable loop quantum cosmology
papers.abstract: In canonical quantum gravity the physical states solve the constraints but are typically not normalizable in the kinematical Hilbert space. Group averaging constructs them from normalizable kinematical seeds. We describe the geometry of this seed-to-state map in the language of geometric quantum mechanics. When averaging is an orthogonal projection, the admissible kinematical rays form a holomorphic vector bundle over the physical ray space. The embedded exact solutions form its zero section, and its fibers are strictly larger than gauge orbits. Observables descend to the base exactly when the Hessian of the squared constraint vanishes along their flow. For distributional physical states, group averaging on an explicit Sobolev test space yields an affine bundle of representatives. Its sections are embeddings of the physical ray space whose images contain no exact solutions. The test-space inner product singles out one of them, and narrowing the seed profile gives Weyl sequences of approximate solutions. We apply this to solvable loop quantum cosmology. Group averaging reproduces the Klein--Gordon physical inner product on an explicit test space. Because the scalar-field momentum enters the constraint quadratically, the constraint spectrum has an edge near the shell. The canonical section is then mode-dependent and not Kähler isometric, and the canonical seeds of small universes are biased off the shell. The edge also separates the Page--Wootters state from the slice of the Klein--Gordon solution. An ideal clock shows none of these effects. The results separate the canonical structures, namely physical rays, physical geometry and Dirac observables, from those that depend on a choice of seeds, test space or clock.

papers.title: Regular magnetic black holes with anti-de Sitter cores in scalar-tensor gravity: axial stability and radial instability
papers.abstract: We construct static, asymptotically flat regular black holes in Einstein-frame scalar--tensor gravity, sourced by a canonical scalar coupled to magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics. Prescribing the density and scalar profiles, we reconstruct the metric, the scalar--photon coupling and the potential. Regularity requires the mass function to vanish at the centre, which fixes the ADM mass, and the central $r^2$ growth of the density to be compensated by the gradient energy of the scalar. The solutions have an anti-de Sitter core supported by a negative potential and a nearly Reissner--Nordström exterior; absence of ghosts restricts the magnetic charge to an interval that shrinks to zero at a finite core depth. Axial perturbations reduce to a symmetric two-channel master system whose positive-definite potential guarantees mode stability; spectral and time-domain quasinormal frequencies agree. Radial perturbations, by contrast, are unstable: the reconstructed potential behaves as $V\propto-\varphi^5$ near the asymptotic vacuum, the scalar becomes tachyonic outside the horizon, and every ghost-free black hole has a growing monopole mode with $\Gamma M\approx0.14$--$0.28$. An angular Laplacian instability develops near the centre; for black holes it may lie entirely within the inner horizon, while horizonless solutions leave it uncovered and are therefore excluded.

papers.title: The MAGE Project: Size Evolution and Disk Formation in Massive Galaxies at Cosmic Dawn
papers.abstract: We investigate size evolution and disk formation with a new suite of eleven cosmological zoom-in simulations, Massive Assembly of Galaxies in the Early universe (MAGE), run with RAMSES at $\sim10\,\mathrm{pc}$ resolution until $z\simeq9$. The target galaxies span stellar masses of $M_\star\simeq2\times10^8$-$3\times10^{10}\,M_\odot$ at $z=9$. The stellar half-mass radius grows steeply with stellar mass at low masses, turns over near $M_\star\simeq5\times10^9\,M_\odot$, and evolves weakly with redshift. The intrinsic UV sizes in MAGE overlap the compact end of observed distributions, including the compact strong-line systems, but not the more extended population at $z>9$. Dust, PSF-limited size measurements, and our overdense environments may contribute to this offset. In the simulations, stars dominate the mass within the half-mass radius above $M_\star\simeq5\times10^8\,M_\odot$, where the central circular speed exceeds a characteristic stellar-feedback scale. Outflows are then increasingly retained within the galaxy, consistent with gas recycling on galactic rather than halo scales, which sustains central gas supply and drives a compaction-like central buildup. The turnover in size at $M_\star\simeq5\times10^9\,M_\odot$ coincides with rapid growth of rotational support to $v/\sigma\simeq1.5$-$3$ in star-forming gas and stars younger than 10Myr, as the central circular speed exceeds the halo virial speed, which the star-forming gas velocity dispersion tracks. The subsequent low central gas fraction, declining central star formation, and younger outskirts suggest the onset of inside-out quenching.
papers.comments: 31 pages, 15 figures, submitted to MNRAS, comments are welcome!

papers.title: Ricci-flat Seeds, Trombone Rescaling and Magnetizing Kerr Black Holes
papers.abstract: We present a new family of Ricci-flat rotating metrics, which we refer to as Solution II, obtained by demagnetizing the genuine Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (G-KBR) black hole. Together with Solution I, which was previously obtained by demagnetizing the Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (KBR) black hole, this gives two families of Ricci-flat deformations of the Kerr black hole, each labeled by $B$. We study the global structures, thermodynamics, various limits, and the local connections among these limits. We also study the remagnetizations in both Einstein-Maxwell and Kaluza-Klein theories, and find that, to yield a physically acceptable solution, the Ernst transformation should be augmented by an appropriate trombone rescaling.
papers.comments: Latex, 34 pages, typos, signs and coefficients are corrected, metric functions are significantly simplified

papers.title: A cosmological intercept tension in local distance ladders
papers.abstract: The Hubble tension motivates direct tests of the internal consistency of the local distance ladder. We perform forward and backward consistency checks between Type Ia supernovae in Cepheid host galaxies and the Hubble-flow supernova sample using Pantheon+ data. Within flat $\Lambda$CDM, we impose Planck-CMB priors on one sample, infer the supernova absolute-magnitude calibration, and propagate it to the other sample to recover the Hubble constant, which should match the input value if the second and third rungs of the distance ladder align perfectly. We examine the impact of host-galaxy peculiar velocities using redshift corrections based on the Manticore-Local reconstruction. These corrections shift the recovered $H_0$ from $74.30^{+1.18}_{-1.20}$ to $71.37^{+1.23}_{-1.18}$ $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ in the forward analysis and from $60.83^{+0.98}_{-0.97}$ to $63.25^{+0.95}_{-0.93}$ $\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}Mpc^{-1}}$ in the backward analysis, bringing both results closer to the input CMB constraint. Comparing the cosmological intercepts of the magnitude-redshift relation inferred from two rungs of the distance ladder before and after peculiar-velocity corrections, we find that the significance of the discrepancy decreases from $6.8\sigma$ to $3.9\sigma$ in the forward check and from $7.3\sigma$ to $4.3\sigma$ in the backward check. Peculiar-velocity corrections therefore partially alleviate the intercept tension, while the residual discrepancy is further cut in half by volumetric bias down to $\sim1.7\sigma$. Our results highlight the importance of local velocity modeling and motivate further tests of sample selection and calibration systematics in assessing distance-ladder consistency.
papers.comments: v1, 7 pages, 2 figures; v2, 10 pages, 5 figures, this http URL added to address volumetric bias

papers.title: An Extra-nuclear Water Maser in NGC 1106 Likely Driven By An AGN Shock: Implications for Maser-based Black Hole Mass Measurements
papers.abstract: We present Very Large Array A-configuration ($0.13$'') 22 GHz spectral-line and continuum observations of the Swift-BAT detected Seyfert 2 galaxy, NGC 1106, aimed at localizing a water maser line offset from the host systemic velocity by 541 km s$^{-1}$. The 22 GHz continuum emission reveals a 352 pc extended structure within the nucleus of NGC 1106, and we spatially resolve the water maser emission to a compact region $\sim1$ kpc ($3.12$'') from the nucleus. Comparing our data with previous 22 GHz 1'' observations, we found that the water maser lies near the boundary of a radio extension aligned with the jet axis, likely arising from the interface between the active galactic nucleus (AGN) outflow and the host galaxy's ISM. To verify this, we compared the water maser in NGC 1106 to a known water maser in a star-forming region within the Milky Way, along with known extragalactic water masers associated with star formation and AGN driven outflows. Overall, we found that the maser position, velocity offset, flux density, and alignment with the jet axis are consistent with an origin at the interface between the AGN outflow and the host ISM. Our results have important implications for maser-based black hole mass measurements in which disk geometry is ambiguous. Since single-dish observations cannot spatially separate disk masers from outflow-driven masers, high-velocity maser features attributed to the accretion disk may also include contributions from kpc-scale shocks.
papers.comments: Accepted to ApJ, 11 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables

papers.title: Gravitational-Wave Signatures and Periodic Orbits of Charged Particles Around a Five-Dimensional Rotating Black Hole: Comparison with the Kerr Black Hole
papers.abstract: We study periodic orbits of charged particles in the equatorial plane of a five-dimensional ($D=5$) rotating Myers--Perry black hole (BH) immersed in a uniform magnetic field, and the gravitational waves emitted by these orbits in an extreme mass-ratio inspiral. All results are compared with the Kerr BH in the uniform magnetic field. We find that a charged particle is much more weakly bound to the $D=5$ dimensional BH, i.e. its energy at the innermost stable circular orbit is close to unity, $0.95$--$0.99$, compared with $0.78$--$0.94$ for the Kerr BH, and the depth of the potential well is several times smaller. As a result, the periodic orbits of the $D=5$ dimensional BH lie much closer to the separatrix. The magnetic field can make the azimuthal frequency of the orbit smaller than the radial one and produces loops in the orbits far from the BH. Using the numerical kludge method, we compute the gravitational waveforms for a compact object of $10M_\odot$ orbiting a BH of $10^6M_\odot$. At the same magnetic field, the $D=5$ dimensional signal has a longer period, lower frequencies, and an amplitude smaller by about $18\%$. We show that for the magnetic parameter $\beta M=0.02$ the strongest spectral line is at $7.9$\,mHz, compared with $9.9$\,mHz for the Kerr BH. An estimate of the radiation reaction shows that the periodic orbits survive from less than an hour to a few days in the presence of an external magnetic field. Over these lifetimes, the signal-to-noise ratio for LISA is $7$--$31$ for the rotating BH in $D=5$ dimensions, compared to the Kerr BH where it is about $15$--$54$.

papers.title: What sets the star-formation rate in the Milky Way? I. A multi-scale view of the star-formation rate
papers.abstract: Context. The star-formation rate (SFR) is one of the key quantities that characterizes the star formation process and has been extensively investigated both observationally and theoretically. Aims. We aim to provide a coherent multi-scale view of star formation by connecting Galactic-scale conditions (kpc) to the properties of individual star-forming clumps at sub-parsec scales. Methods. We perform a set of numerical simulations with large-scale turbulent forcing designed to reproduce physical conditions typical of the solar neighbourhood. Using adaptive zooming down to 0.03 pc, we obtain a population of star-forming clumps that is analyzed and compared with observational catalogues in a companion paper. Results. For column densities and velocity dispersions consistent with Galactic values, the resulting SFR is close to the rate inferred for the Milky Way. Comparing this value with the SFR expected from pure free-fall collapse shows that turbulence provides multiscale support that lowers the SFR by more than an order of magnitude. Additional regulation by stellar feedback, including ionizing radiation and protostellar outflows, likely reduces the SFR by an additional factor of 3-10. Comparisons with observations across multiple spatial scales show good overall agreement with this model. Conclusions. These results support a picture in which turbulence plays a central role in regulating star formation in the Milky Way. In combination with stellar feedback, it limits the star formation efficiency to only a few percent. Key words. stars: formation -- ISM: clouds -- physical processes: turbulence

papers.title: The Role of Star Formation and Morphology in the Mass-Metallicity Relation of Galaxies at Cosmic Noon
papers.abstract: We investigate the dependence of the mass-metallicity relation (MZR) on star formation and galaxy morphology at 1.7<z<3.5, using JWST/NIRISS wide-field slitless spectroscopy of >1000 galaxies. The observations span >85 arcmin^2 from the pure-parallel PASSAGE and OutThere surveys. We derive gas-phase metallicities using a Bayesian framework that combines multiple strong emission-line ratios calibrated against direct auroral-line metallicity measurements from JWST. We constrain stellar masses, star formation rates (SFRs), and morphological properties using ancillary HST and JWST imaging. We stack spectra by stellar mass to constrain the MZR over log(M*/M)~6.5-11, and find that it is well described by a second-order polynomial, with a steep low-mass slope and metallicities<10% solar at log(M*/M)<7.5. Additional stacking by SFR and morphology reveals strong evidence for a fundamental metallicity relation (FMR). Specifically, at log(M*/M)<9.5, galaxies with lower SFRs are more metal-rich than those with higher SFRs at fixed mass. At log(M*/M)<9.5, we find that larger galaxies, and those having lower SFR surface densities, bulges, and/or spiral features are significantly metal rich relative to their smaller, higher SFR surface density, bulge-less, and/or non-spiral counterparts. These results suggest the secondary dependencies of the MZR reflect variations in the baryon cycle, such that recent metal-poor gas accretion drives concentrated star formation and metallicity dilution, while structurally developed galaxies retain more chemically enriched gas reservoirs.
papers.comments: Submitted to ApJ. Main text has 22 pages, including 10 figures. Comments welcome
